newsitem.title: UK: Taylor sees contracting pain continuing.
newsitem.headline: Taylor sees contracting pain continuing.

text.p: Taylor Woodrow Plc, the building to property group, warned on Tuesday that the pain in the contracting industry was set to continue, with margins coming under pressure both in the UK and abroad.

Chairman Colin Parsons said at a results press briefing that he saw contracting as the smallest contributor of future growth, but said the company was committed to remain in the sector. The key engines of future growth were housing and land development, followed by property and Greenham Trading.
"Contracting will not be seeing any big improvement in earnings. We will not see the big money of a few years ago," said Parsons.
But he emphasised the group's commitment to keeping all four businesses, likening them to the sturdiness of four legs on a chair.
"It's like sitting on a chair instead of relying on the uncomfortable shooting stick of having just one business."
Parsons also criticised the delays in awarding contracts under the private finance initiative (PFI).
"PFI will come good in the long run. But...it has a gestation period akin to the pregnancy of an elephant."
The initiative is a flagship government policy to get private money into public infrastructure projects, but has come under attack for its expense, delays and bureacracy.
The delays have partly led to a dearth of new construction projects in a market already suffering from a lack of demand.
